_what_this_is: The external pin on the law's own bytes AND on everything that decides whether the law runs or what it reads. ROUND 49 (CD-48-01) pinned the two law files: the caller could no longer skip the audit, because any edit to the law moved a digest here. ROUND 50 closes the two rungs above that, both measured as fail-opens. The coordinator's CD-49-01 (P1): nothing pinned COLLECTION, so one line in vitest.config.ts, one flag in package.json's test script, or a testNamePattern left the law uncollected with a green suite and an untouched pin (278 passed with a plant); the pin now covers vitest.config.ts, package.json, both tsconfigs and every tools/ file the law executes, and tools/law-ran.py runs OUTSIDE the suite as its own npm script and refuses by name (LAW-NOT-RUN) when the law's cases did not run. The challenger's R48-F3 (P1): nothing pinned what the law READS as configuration, so one appended enrolment line in tools/reviewer-reports.json exempted a planted document at 303 passed — camouflaged as the bookkeeping every round does — so that file is pinned here, its entries must be reviewer-shaped names carrying a sha256, and an enrolled report's bytes are verified against it. THE DECLARED LIMIT, unchanged in shape: an edit to a pinned file AND to this pin together passes, bounded by review of the diff, where it is a changed digest sitting beside the change it licenses. A PIN CANNOT PIN ITSELF: this file's own bytes are not hashed here, and what stands in for that is the SET check on both sides (dropping a row refuses by name in both files) plus that same review. Updating a digest here is a deliberate act with a visible diff line, and the commit message must say why.
